Essays by Rohan Mahtani

Life and
career strategy.

On making decisions, understanding yourself,
and getting better at the things that matter to you.

Hey, I’m Rohan!

I run Coached, the behavioral science lab, and Resume Worded, a tool for job seekers.

I write these a few times a month.

More about me

Getting past nerves

Why you never stop being nervous

Why practice doesn’t always make the nerves go away—and what helps instead.

I get nervous more than you'd think. I've sent about 350 of these newsletters and I often still get a knot in my stomach before each one goes out. I feel the same right before a big presentation, or a meeting with someone "important".

Read the essay
5 min
Making a decision

How I deal with regret in my career

A way to make today’s decisions by asking what you’d regret later.

In 1994, Jeff was at a crossroads.

He’d recently been promoted to senior VP at an investment bank (the youngest in the firm's history), and was earning handsomely.

But something gnawed at him:

The internet was growing 2,000% a year, and he couldn’t stop thinking about quitting to start a virtual bookstore.

Read the essay
3 min
Working with people

How approachable are YOU?

The opportunities you miss when people hesitate to start a conversation with you.

A huge part of your career (and life, honestly) depends on random conversations:

  • Airbnb started because after a design class, Joe Gebbia went up to speak to Brian Chesky, who became his co-founder.

  • A friend of mine struck up a conversation with someone at a mutual friend’s birthday party — they now have two kids.

  • Or even personally: One of my closest friends and collaborators today is someone I randomly started talking to at a coffee shop.

Read the essay
